conviction_note: The two measurements lean the same way at small size. The findings sum to +1.0: an easy Q3 comp and a low EPS bar (consensus $0.00) beat a sector destocking proxy and a guided H2 cost ramp. On the scaled side, abs_move is 18% (implied 23.5% but the ATM spread is 40% of mid; the median reaction is 14.6%) and p_up is 55, giving (2*0.55-1)*18 = +1.8. p_up stays close to 50 because most of the positive case is inference from primary documents, not an unseen number, and because this name trades on the guide and the guide was just raised.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $80.8M, EPS $0.00, whisper $0.01. Source: Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-28 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/HNST/22305). The company's own FY2026 guide is consistent with this: revenue $319-325M less H1 $161.4M leaves $157.6-163.6M for H2, about $79-82M a quarter. The same guide sets adjusted EBITDA at $23-25M; H1 reported $18.45M (Q1 $3.95M + Q2 $14.5M including $6.6M of tariff refunds), so H2 implied is $4.6-6.6M. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530979/000162828026053315/honestcoq2-26exhibit991.htm. Earnings Whispers quotes FY revenue consensus near $309M, below the guided low end; this most likely reflects estimates excluding the ~$10M apparel liquidation. So the FY revenue bar is disputed by about $10M and the Q3 bar is not.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/hnst/shortinterest, read 2026-11-05): 9.46M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 8.8% of 107.3M shares outstanding, 6.97 days to cover. That is down from 10.73M on 2026-08-31, so the short is moderate, not crowded, and has been covering into the print. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so the market makes no directional statement through skew. Put/call open interest is 0.27, which is call-heavy. Options: ATM IV 122%, event-implied move 23.5%, ATM spread 40% of mid, so the implied move is indicative only. Tape: -11.7% over 20 days, -4.4% over 5 days, -26% from the 52-week high, +109% from the 52-week low.

findings.finding: Q3 has the easiest organic comparison of the year. Q3 2025 organic revenue was $72.6M, down 4.7% year on year on diaper weakness. Q2 2026 organic growth accelerated to +6.7% (Q1 +3.9%), wipes consumption grew ~26% against ~2% for the category, and total tracked consumption grew 7.7% against 2.3%. Holding the Q2 pace gives Q3 organic of about $77.4M; with the remaining apparel liquidation (~$7M of the ~$10M guided is still to come after $3.1M in Q2), reported revenue lands at or above the $80.8M consensus. High-single-digit organic growth would still sit inside the upper end of the raised 5-7% FY guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Organic acceleration plus a raised guide bought +40.8% on 2026-08-05 and +10.0% on 2026-05-06 (baseline). A diaper-driven organic miss with a guide cut sold -29.4% on 2025-11-05.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $80.8M is down 12.8% year on year, which models the exits rather than an organic acceleration on a -4.7% base. If the market priced Q3 organic at Q2's pace or better on the easy comp, the stock would not have drifted -11.7% over 20 days to the bottom of its post-Q2 range ($4.46-6.01 per Earnings Whispers). It is partly priced, because the raised FY organic guide already implies H2 growth of roughly 5-8.5%.
findings.independence: Consumption and organic numbers come from the Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530979/000162828026053315/honestcoq2-26exhibit991.htm) and Pulse 2.0 (https://pulse2.com/honest-company-consumption-grows-7-7-versus-2-3-category-growth-as-organic-revenue-rises-6-7/). Both are company-reported; there is no independent scanner series.

findings.finding: Further IEEPA tariff refunds may land in Q3 and are not in the balance sheet. The Q2 10-Q shows $11.9M received in Q2 ($6.6M booked against cost of revenue, $0.5M as interest income, $0.6M against inventory), no receivable recognised for future refunds because timing and recoverability were uncertain, and a $4.2M liability to contract manufacturers. CBP told the CIT on 2026-09-15 that about $122B had been certified and sent to Treasury for payment, and opened CAPE Phase 3 for liquidated entries on 2026-10-06. Any Q3 refunds would be recognised on receipt, on top of a $0.00 EPS consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print carried $6.6M of refunds (790bp of gross margin) and the stock rose +40.8%. The company also reported underlying EBITDA ex-refunds and raised its organic guide, so the refund was not the line that print traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.00 against $0.04 in Q2 implies the Street models no Q3 refund. If a Q3 refund were expected, the Q3 EPS bar would sit above breakeven.
findings.independence: CBP progress comes from C.H. Robinson (https://www.chrobinson.com/en-us/resources/insights-and-advisories/client-advisories/2026q3/09-17-26-cbp-cape-phase-3-ieepa-refunds/, 2026-09-17). It is a separate source but a proxy: nothing confirms that Honest has remaining eligible entries.

findings.finding: The $25M buyback authorised on 2026-02-20 was fully used by 2026-08-05 (about 5.6M shares at $3.35 in H1, the rest after June). The company holds $105.9M of cash with no debt, about 22% of a ~$471M market cap at $4.39. No new authorisation 8-K has been filed since, so a new programme could come with the print, as the last one came around the Q4 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior authorisation (2026-02-20) came with the Q4 2025 print of 2026-02-25, which reacted +20.8% (baseline), alongside guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference, not an announced fact. A priced new buyback would show up as support near the post-Q2 low, and the stock is sitting at that low.
findings.independence: The EDGAR submissions list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001530979.json) shows no 8-K after 2026-08-05. Same company document set; no outside confirmation.

findings.finding: A competitor counterparty that reported after Honest last spoke shows Q3 retailer destocking and promotional pressure. Kimberly-Clark North America Q3 2026: organic +0.4%, volume +2.0%, net price about -1.8% from 'increased promotional activity', and retailer inventory timing cutting organic sales by about 130bp. P&G's quarter to 2026-09-30 shows North America Baby Care up only low single digits with lower pricing. Honest's diapers (about $20M a quarter, already down 21% in Q2 after distribution losses at two large customers) sit in the most promoted category, and retailer destocking would hit shipments against consumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Diaper weakness drove the Q3 2025 miss and guide cut (-29.4%) and the -17.3% reaction of 2025-08-06. Since then diapers have been guided as a declining drag and the stock has risen through it on wipes and personal care.
findings.why_not_priced: KMB reported this morning, after the Earnings Whispers preview and after any Honest estimate revisions. If the market were transferring the destocking to HNST it would show as weakness today. The stock is -4.4% over 5 days, which partly fits. Net of the rest of the company: wipes and personal care are over 70% of revenue and grew ~26% in consumption, so the diaper and destocking drag has to overcome that.
findings.independence: P&G 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-09-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080424/000008042426000256/pg-20260930.htm): lower North America baby care pricing. Both are proxies; Honest itself has not confirmed destocking.

findings.finding: Management guided to a costlier second half: marketing up about 20% in H2, SG&A investment ramping, and part of the $35.3M H1 cash inflow (inventory timing; inventory fell to $49.7M from $72.5M) expected to partly reverse. The FY adjusted EBITDA guide of $23-25M implies H2 of only $4.6-6.6M if it includes the Q2 refunds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed directly. Profit-reinvestment framing accompanied the +40.8% Q2 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the company's own guidance, and the $0.00 EPS consensus reflects it. The residual risk is a Q3 EBITDA print below the implied H2 run rate, or a cash flow reversal larger than flagged.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530979/000162828026053315/honestcoq2-26exhibit991.htm) gives the EBITDA guide and the inventory figures, so this shares documents with finding 1's bar.

findings.finding: The stock has de-rated into the print without a filed cause: -11.7% over 20 days and -4.4% over 5 days to $4.39, below the $4.46 bottom of its post-Q2 range. Short interest fell from 10.73M (2026-08-31) to 9.46M (2026-10-15), and option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.27).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints reacted +40.8%, +10.0% and +20.8%. The five before were all negative.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is filed only because the expectation reset makes the bar easier to clear; an unexplained drawdown is not evidence.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline tape and options block (run_up_20d_pct -11.67, put_call_open_interest_ratio 0.27). Same data family.

findings.finding: EDGAR shows a cluster of Form 144s and Form 4s after the Q2 print: seven Form 144s on 2026-08-20/21, seven Form 4s on 2026-08-24, and a Form 144 on 2026-10-08 followed by a Form 4 for Thomas Sternweis on 2026-10-09. The transaction detail could not be read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A similar post-print Form 4 cluster on 2026-05-22 preceded the +40.8% Q2 reaction, so the pattern looks routine and has not been predictive.
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public. The clustering after each print points to open-window or RSU-vest sales, which the market typically ignores.
